teaser.text: Wheaton Precious Metals is a financier of mines that turns rights to future metal into sales. To understand how a dollar moves through it, follow the contract from the mine owner to the metal buyer, then separate the operating spread from the investment that made it possible.

blocks.heading: Where could Wheaton's shares go in the forecast?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted price is CAD 192.55 in October 2027, CAD 202.79 in October 2028, and CAD 223.19 in October 2029. Including dividends, those outcomes represent approximately 0%, 6% and 17% from today’s CAD 194.06. By October 2029, the bear case reaches CAD 103.31 while the bull case reaches CAD 423.60.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Wheaton?

paragraphs.text: The November 6, 2026 third-quarter call should test whether Salobo and Peñasquito improve, Antamina ships a full quarter and debt begins to fall. Koné’s hard-rock circuit is scheduled for Q2 2027. Spring Valley targets first gold in the first half of 2028, close to the April 2028 term-loan maturity. Reliable Antamina shipments and timely project ramps through 2027–2028 support the bull case; delays or weaker prices slow debt repayment. The investment turns on reliable Antamina shipments, on-time project ramps and falling debt before April 2028.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Wheaton really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending of US$1,341,369 thousand in 2025 left free cash flow of US$563,107 thousand after lease payments. After deducting stock compensation as an economic cost, real free cash flow was US$556,632 thousand. The five-year record is lumpy because stream purchases and milestone payments arrive irregularly.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Wheaton today?

paragraphs.text: EV/EBITDA compares enterprise value with earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and depletion. Wheaton’s reported multiple is 22.98x, but adding depletion back does not make the original purchase free. Operating cash can also be committed to new streams: existing contracts generated US$650 million of operating cash flow in the second quarter of 2026, while upfront stream payments reached US$4.5 billion. That helps explain a thin free-cash-flow yield and a dividend yield that leaves the investment case dependent mainly on future growth.

blocks.heading: How much does Wheaton pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Shareholders now have a more predictable claim on that cash. Wheaton replaced a dividend tied to 30% of trailing average operating cash flow with a progressive quarterly policy. The dividend began at $0.155 per share and reached $0.195 in 2026. That expectation must coexist with taxes, new streams, debt repayment and weaker metal prices.

blocks.heading: Does Wheaton cover its dividend with cash?

paragraphs.text: Dividends were paid every year from 2021 through 2025, while Wheaton made no share buybacks. In a weaker cash-flow year, dividends exceeded the cash generated in that year, so the company relied on its accumulated reserve. That is manageable for a time, but repeated shortfalls would consume the cash needed for stream funding and debt service.

paragraphs.text: Wheaton’s weighted return could be roughly flat at the first forecast date and 17% higher at the last, including dividends, if deliveries support growth and cash repays debt. Management guides to 860,000–940,000 GEOs in 2026. GEOs are gold-equivalent ounces, combining different metals by their gold value. Management said 3.0% of forecast production would come from assets in construction or ramp-up.

Management reaffirmed its 2026 production guidance in August. The first half produced approximately 415,000 GEOs, leaving a substantial second-half increase to reach the target. Salobo and Peñasquito sequencing, plus a full quarter from the Antamina stream, are expected to do most of the work. Only 3.0% of forecast annual production comes from assets still being built or ramped up.

blocks.heading: Did Wheaton keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: There is evidence of delivery. Wheaton’s February 2026 production update confirmed that 2025 output exceeded guidance. The CFO transition occurred in 2025, and the CEO transition followed in 2026. Those results support credit for execution, while the longer test of future investment returns remains open.

blocks.heading: What are Wheaton's last eight quarters of results?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached US$929,201 thousand, against US$503,218 thousand in Q2 2025. Net income rose from US$292,270 thousand to US$543,236 thousand. Operating cash flow also increased, but the operating explanation was smaller than the revenue headline: production grew about 6%, while sales volumes grew about 14%. Realized GEO prices grew about 61%, so the market did most of the work.

The sequential comparison was weaker. Gross margin fell from 77.6% to 74.0%, and operating income slipped from US$674,793 thousand to US$667,058 thousand. New finance costs and the first substantial global-minimum-tax cash payment added pressure to cash generation.
